author: code-quality-reviewer

findings.description: The local variable `requestedPage` actually holds the clamped/effective page (Math.max(page, FIRST_PAGE)), not the raw value the client requested — the raw request is still held by the `page` parameter one line above. A future reader skimming this method will read `requestedPage` as 'what the client asked for' and be misled, especially since the surrounding comment already explains the normalisation. Name the variable for what it is.
findings.fix: Rename `requestedPage` to something that names the post-clamp value, e.g. `effectivePage` or `normalizedPage`, and update its two use sites (the `findPaginatedForOwnersLastName` and `addPaginationModel` calls).

findings.description: `FIRST_PAGE` now does double duty: it is both the lower-bound clamp value (`Math.max(page, FIRST_PAGE)`) and the 1-based-to-0-based conversion offset (`page - FIRST_PAGE`). The two are numerically the same today only because the listing's first page happens to be 1. A reader who changes the clamp boundary for an unrelated reason (e.g. a future 0-indexed URL scheme) will silently break the `PageRequest` conversion here, because nothing at this line signals that the subtraction is doing index conversion rather than reusing the boundary constant. The class javadoc on `FIRST_PAGE` documents the second role but this call site doesn't point back to it.
findings.fix: Add a short inline comment at this line (or in the constant's javadoc) making the dual role explicit, e.g. 'FIRST_PAGE also serves as the 1-based-to-0-based offset because the listing's first page is 1' — or, if that coupling feels too implicit, introduce a distinct named conversion instead of reusing the boundary constant for arithmetic.

approved_aspects: Clamping once at the HTTP boundary (top of processFindForm) rather than inside findPaginatedForOwnersLastName is the right call: page also drives addPaginationModel's currentPage attribute, and clamping only in the query helper would leave the view claiming 'page 0' while the query silently served page 1 — the chosen placement keeps both consumers of `page` consistent with a single normalisation.
FIRST_PAGE replacing the bare `- 1` literal is a real readability improvement, with a javadoc that correctly explains the 1-based vs 0-based indexing.
The explanatory comment above the clamp states rationale ('so anything below the first page is normalised here rather than rejected') rather than restating the code — matches house commenting style.
checkFormat passes clean; no formatting or checkstyle issues introduced.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Boundary normalization is complete for the lower bound: `Math.max(page, FIRST_PAGE)` in OwnerController.processFindForm runs before any use of the parameter, and both downstream consumers (findPaginatedForOwnersLastName and addPaginationModel) receive the clamped `requestedPage`, so no unclamped value survives past the boundary. No arithmetic overflow path exists: the clamped value is >= 1, so `page - FIRST_PAGE` is >= 0 and Integer.MAX_VALUE is unaffected.

Error surface is not widened: the fix removes a reachable IllegalArgumentException (previously a 500 via templates/error.html) and replaces it with a normal 200 listing. `server.error.include-message` is left at the Spring Boot default (`never`), so the error template's `${message}` slot was already empty; no internal detail was disclosed before and none is now. An unauthenticated caller learns strictly less, not more.

Deferred item 1 (no upper-bound clamp on `page`) is correctly out of scope for security. A page beyond the last yields an empty Page, which takes the `rejectValue("lastName", "notFound")` branch and returns 200 with the find form -- no exception, no stack trace, no data disclosure. The only residual effect is a deep-OFFSET query cost, which is a resource-consumption concern, not a disclosure or integrity defect, and it is identical to the pre-change baseline.

Deferred item 2 (non-numeric `page` becoming a binding failure) is correctly out of scope for security. `@RequestParam int` raises MethodArgumentTypeMismatchException, which Spring resolves to 400 with the message suppressed by the default `include-message=never`; the attacker-controlled string is not reflected. This path is unchanged by the diff.

No new injection surface: data access still goes through the derived repository query `findByLastNameStartingWith(String, Pageable)` with a bound parameter -- no concatenated query text was introduced. No template escaping was disabled; `currentPage` is an int, so the Thymeleaf preprocessing expressions in owners/ownersList.html (`__${currentPage - 1}__`) cannot carry request-supplied markup or expression text.

No secrets, credentials, or credential-shaped literals appear in the diff (swept the change set for token/password/secret/key/credential); no new endpoint, no broadened management exposure, no change to the InitBinder disallow list (`id`, `*.id`) that guards mass assignment, and no serialization surface touched.

Supply chain unaffected: `git diff` over build.gradle, gradle.properties, and gradle/ is empty -- the change set is two Java files only, so no new or upgraded dependency enters the graph and no CVE exposure changes with this slice.

Note, not a finding: VetController.showVetList carries the same unclamped `PageRequest.of(page - 1, pageSize)` pattern at src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/vet/VetController.java:61. It is pre-existing, untouched by this change set, and per docs/security-principles.md the pre-existing baseline is not a review finding; its failure mode is likewise a message-suppressed 500 with no disclosure. Recorded for the PRD backlog, not as a blocker on this slice.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: The required behavior is two-sided: 'any page below 1 is treated as the first page' AND 'page >= 1 behavior unchanged'. The new parameterized test pins the first half precisely (asserts currentPage==1 and, via the Pageable captor, that the repository sees page index 0 for inputs 0 and -1). The second half is not pinned anywhere: the pre-existing processFindFormSuccess (line 160, unmodified by this change) calls get("/owners?page=1") but only asserts HTTP status and view name — it never captures the Pageable to check getPageNumber(). No test in the file asserts the repository-facing page index for any page>=1 (not even page=1, let alone page=2). A future regression in the FIRST_PAGE arithmetic (e.g. `page - FIRST_PAGE` accidentally changed to `page` or to a hardcoded index) that only affects the page>=1 branch would pass the full suite today.
findings.fix: Add a Pageable captor assertion to processFindFormSuccess (or add a dedicated theOwnerListingShouldKeepPagesFromOneUnchanged-style test at page=2) asserting pageable.getValue().getPageNumber() equals the expected zero-based index, mirroring the captor pattern already used in theOwnerListingShouldTreatAPageBelowOneAsTheFirstPage.

approved_aspects: theOwnerListingShouldTreatAPageBelowOneAsTheFirstPage pins actual behavior, not just absence-of-exception: it asserts both the currentPage model attribute and, via an ArgumentCaptor on the existing MockitoBean OwnerRepository, that the repository is queried with zero-based page index 0 for both page=0 and page=-1 inputs

Mocking stays within policy: MockMvc is the sanctioned transport double, and the ArgumentCaptor rides on the OwnerRepository MockitoBean that was already established in this test class (no new mocking surface introduced)
BDD test name (theOwnerListingShouldTreatAPageBelowOneAsTheFirstPage) follows the brief's naming school for tests modified after 2026-07-31
FIRST_PAGE / FIRST_PAGE_INDEX are meaningful, role-named Tier-1 constants mirroring the production constant added in OwnerController, eliminating mystery literals
@ParameterizedTest with @ValueSource correctly covers both boundary values (0 and -1) instead of a single spot-check
./gradlew test passes with the new test included

rationale: fix contained to reviewed surface; dissenters re-review the delta

author: code-quality-reviewer
approved_aspects: requestedPage renamed to effectivePage at all three use sites, matching the norm the rest of the method already used

FIRST_PAGE dual-role concern: the implementer's rebuttal holds on its merits — if the first page is numbered FIRST_PAGE, then index = page - FIRST_PAGE follows by construction for any numbering base, so a future re-basing of FIRST_PAGE cannot desync the two uses the way the original finding worried about; this is not incidental equality, it's the same offset by definition
toPageIndex(int) extraction gives the arithmetic a name and the javadoc states why the offset is FIRST_PAGE, closing the legibility half of the original finding cleanly

author: test-reviewer
approved_aspects: The new theOwnerListingShouldQueryTheZeroBasedIndexOfARequestedPage closes the prior finding: it exercises page in {1,2,5} and, via the pre-existing ArgumentCaptor<Pageable> pattern, asserts both the model's currentPage and the repository-facing pageable.getValue().getPageNumber() against expected indices supplied as CsvSource literals (0,1,4) rather than a re-derivation of page-1/toPageIndex -- so the test would actually fail if the FIRST_PAGE arithmetic regressed for page>=1, which is exactly the gap flagged last round.

Relocating the assertion to a dedicated test rather than adding a captor to processFindFormSuccess is not an evasion: my prior finding explicitly offered both options ('add a Pageable captor assertion to processFindFormSuccess ... or add a dedicated test'), and keeping processFindFormSuccess focused on the multiple-results view while giving page-index conversion its own parameterized test is arguably the cleaner separation -- one behavior per test method, matching the brief's structure guidance.
@ParameterizedTest/@CsvSource is the right tool for three independently meaningful page/index pairs rather than three copy-pasted tests.
Test naming (theOwnerListingShouldQueryTheZeroBasedIndexOfARequestedPage) follows the brief's BDD naming school.
Mocking stays within policy: MockMvc as the sanctioned transport double, ArgumentCaptor riding the already-established OwnerRepository MockitoBean -- no new mocking surface.

FIRST_PAGE_INDEX/FIRST_PAGE tier-1 constants reused rather than reintroducing magic numbers; the CsvSource literals (1,2,5 / 0,1,4) are the only new bare numbers and they are the input/expected pairs under test, not incidental setup data.
./gradlew test passes with the new test included.

author: change-grader
summary: clamp the owner-listing page parameter at the HTTP boundary

blast_radius.note: One production method in one package plus its test class; 2 files, 10 hunks, no sensitive paths, and no schema, config, or dependency changes, so the only behavioral surface is the GET /owners handler.

semantic_surprise.note: Read every hunk: toPageIndex(page) is page minus FIRST_PAGE, numerically identical to the old page minus 1, so pages at or above 1 are unchanged and Math.max only lifts the sub-1 inputs that previously threw; clamping in processFindForm rather than in findPaginatedForOwnersLastName also keeps the currentPage model attribute equal to the page actually fetched, which is what stops ownersList.html rendering a previous link to page=0.

test_adequacy.note: Both directions of the boundary are pinned by MockMvc tests that capture the Pageable and assert the repository-facing page index, with expected indices supplied as CsvSource literals rather than re-derived from the production arithmetic, so a regression in toPageIndex fails the suite instead of moving with it.

reviewer_hedging.note: Round-2 approvals from code-quality and test carry empty findings arrays and prose naming each round-1 finding as closed; security and doc approved the full diff in round 1 and were scoped out of the fix-delta roster by the review plan, which is expected rather than silence.

scope_deviation.note: Zero design revisions, consultations, and build retries; the diff stays inside the owner listing named by the dispatch, and the identical VetController defect was reported rather than opportunistically fixed.

rationale: Contained one-method clamp; the arithmetic is provably unchanged for pages at or above 1 and the tests pin both sides of the boundary against literal expected indices. Merge. One carry-out: the identical live defect at VetController.java:61 is recorded only in .scratch/, which is wiped next slice, so file it durably first.
